rows.title: Forty-first Amendment of the Constitution (Right to Housing) Bill 2026
rows.what: Would amend the Constitution by inserting a new Article 40A dealing with a right to housing.
rows.practical: It would create an explicit constitutional basis for a right to housing, with its meaning and effect determined through constitutional law and interpretation.
rows.context: The Bill is presented in response to the housing crisis and seeks to give housing an express place in the Constitution.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the wording of the proposed right, how enforceable it would be, what duties it could place on the State and how it would interact with existing constitutional rights.

rows.title: Planning and Development (Material Interest) Bill 2026
rows.what: prevent permissions for developments being delayed or frustrated by geographically distant objectors who have no material interest in the development concerned. This is intended to serve the interests of individuals and communities who may benefit from the development concerned. The Bill preserves.
rows.practical: The section also provides that, in the case of a submission, observation or appeal by or on behalf of a natural person, evidence submitted solely for the purpose of establishing that he or she has a material interest in the development concerned will not be made available to the public by a.
rows.context: This is intended to serve the interests of individuals and communities who may benefit from the development concerned.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Antarctic Treaty (Accension and Implementation) Bill 2026
rows.what: The Bill proposes a legal change in the area described by its title: Antarctic Treaty (Accension and Implementation) Bill 2026.
rows.practical: The Bill establishes the legal framework necessary for national implementation, regulation of activities by Irish citizens and bodies in the Antarctic Treaty area, and compliance with international obligations.
rows.context: It designates the Minister for Foreign Affairs as the responsible Minister for all matters relating to the Antarctic Treaty System, including representation at Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meetings (ATCM) and the Committee for Environmental Protection (CEP).
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Housing Loans Regulations (Fresh Start - Buyout) (Amendment) Bill 2026
rows.what: Would extend local-authority housing-loan eligibility to a person remaining in the family home after divorce or legal separation who needs finance to buy out a former partner’s share.
rows.practical: Someone who retains the family home but cannot obtain the necessary mortgage finance could apply to a local authority for a housing loan specifically to complete that buyout.
rows.context: The Bill would amend the Housing Loans Regulations 2021 so this group is expressly included within the eligibility rules for local-authority housing loans.
rows.issues: Second Stage can consider eligibility criteria, affordability and credit assessment, treatment of existing ownership interests, and how the change would operate within the local-authority loan scheme.

rows.title: Electricity Regulation (Amendment) (Standing Charges) Bill 2026
rows.what: This Bill would provide a legislative basis for the CRU to effectively monitor and investigate standing charges.
rows.practical: However, these levies are currently unregulated, with the Commission for Regulation of Utilities confirming to the Oireachtas Climate Committee, that they lack the legal remit to investigate the rates of standing charges being imposed by gas and electricity providers.
rows.context: Standing charges are applied to gas and electricity bills to cover the fixed costs of utility companies connecting and maintaining these services to households.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Irish Language Name and Address of the Person (Length Accent) Bill 2026
rows.what: Bheadh dualgas freisin in aon chonradh nua nó athnuaite don Éirchód meas a léiriú ar na dlíthe maidir le húsáid logainmneacha na Gaeltachta.
rows.practical: Déanann an Bille seo iarracht feidhm phraiticiúil a thabhairt don “cheart (atá) acu ón am a mbeirtear iad ainm a bheith orthu” mar atá leagtha amach in Airteagal 7 de Choinbhinsiún na Náisiún Aontaithe um Chearta an Linbh, daingnithe ag an Stát sa bhliain 1992, trí dhearbhú foirmeálta agus cosaint.
rows.context: Is in Éirinn agus sa Ghaeilge atá an oidhreacht is sine ar domhain maidir le sloinntí, le stair scríofa ag tosú sna 900idí.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, and implementation.

rows.title: Official Languages (Right to Use the Irish Language) (Amendment) Bill 2026
rows.what: Cuireadh cosc ar úsáid na Gaeilge in Éirinn don chéad uair ar an 19ú Aibreán 1367 de réir Reachtanna Chill Chainnigh, a dhaingnigh Rí Shasana Anraí VIII sa bhliain 1537, agus mhair an cosc i bhfeidhm ar feadh breis is leathmhílaois go dtí gur scrios An Gorta Mór pobal labhartha na Gaeilge.
rows.practical: Cé go ndearna Westminster aisghairm ar an gcosc reachtúil sa bhliain 1878, lean na Péindlíthe i bhfeidhm chun úsáid na Gaeilge sna cúirteanna a choiriúlú, rud a d’fhág gur cuireadh Gaeilgeoirí neamhchiontacha chun báis mar a tharla i Mám Trasna, agus níor tharla aisghairm ar an dlí sin ó thuaidh go.
rows.context: Alt 2: Leathnaítear cumhachtaí an Choimisinéara Teanga anseo chun imscrúdú agus tuarascáil a dhéanamh ar ghearáin faoi sháruithe ar an gceart chun an Ghaeilge a úsáid agus aithnítear ceart chun an Ghaeilge a úsáid san fhoráil seo agus tugtar cosaint ar leith dá húsáid san ionad oibre, ag tabhairt.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, and implementation.

rows.title: Online Safety (Recommender Algorithms) Bill 2026
rows.what: amend the Online Safety and Media Regulation Act 2022 to regulate the use of recommender algorithms/ systems by video-sharing platform services, including by: prohibiting the use of recommender algorithms for users under 18, or whose age is unknown; prohibiting the use of recommender algorithms.
rows.practical: Prohibits the use of recommender systems for users under 18, or whose age is unknown; prohibits the use of recommender systems based on profiling or sensitive personal data unless the user is over 18, has selected a recommender system based on profiling or sensitive personal data, and has been.
rows.context: Defines video-sharing platform services, recommender systems and profiling using the meanings assigned to them in the Online Safety and Media Regulation Act 2022, the EU Digital Services Act and the EU GDPR directive.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Repeal of Exempted Development Regulations Bill 2026
rows.what: Would repeal two planning exemptions introduced in 2022 and 2023 for buildings used as temporary accommodation for people seeking international protection or receiving temporary protection.
rows.practical: Existing accommodation relying on those exemptions could need to be regularised through the planning system. A transitional provision would allow the responsible State agency to seek retention permission.
rows.context: The Bill specifically targets S.I. 605/2022 and S.I. 376/2023, which created and extended exempted-development treatment for certain temporary accommodation.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine planning oversight, transitional arrangements for existing accommodation, effects on State accommodation capacity, and local planning requirements.

rows.title: Public Art Mural (Exempted Development) Bill 2026
rows.what: Would create planning exemptions for certain public art murals where specified conditions are met.
rows.practical: Qualifying murals could proceed without planning permission where they have artistic or cultural merit, have the building owner’s permission and are not commercial advertising.
rows.context: The Bill would change planning rules that currently govern when murals and similar works require permission.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the qualifying criteria, definitions of artistic or cultural merit, local oversight and how heritage or amenity concerns would be handled.

rows.title: Harassment, Harmful Communications and Related Offences (Amendment) Bill 2026
rows.what: Would amend the Harmful Communications and Related Offences Act 2020 by prohibiting the creation of non-consensual intimate images and increasing penalties for existing offences.
rows.practical: It would add a new prohibition on creating non-consensual images, raise penalties under sections 3 and 4 of the 2020 Act, and extend the time allowed to begin summary proceedings.
rows.context: The Bill is aimed at strengthening the existing legal framework for harmful communications and image-based abuse, including conduct that may occur before an image is distributed.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine the definition of non-consensual creation, evidential requirements, proportionality of penalties, limitation periods and overlap with existing offences.

rows.title: Universal Access to Social Housing (Abolition of Income Limits) Bill 2026
rows.what: provide for universal access to social housing by abolishing income-related criteria.
rows.practical: Provides for the Act to enter into force within 90 days of being promulgated by the President.
rows.context: Amends the Housing (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2009 to delete all the clauses that base social housing assessments on household income or receipt of Rent Supplement, thereby abolishing the income limits for social housing to enable universal access.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, and implementation.

rows.title: Education (Leave for Injuries) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would set minimum standards for any injury-leave scheme maintained by the Minister for Education for teachers and special needs assistants who suffer certain injuries.
rows.practical: The scheme would have to cover matters including medical expenses, certified paid leave, support services, possible early retirement for long-term incapacity and equal treatment of teachers and SNAs.
rows.context: The Bill seeks to put baseline protections around injury leave where a teacher or SNA is hurt or becomes ill in circumstances connected with their work.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine which injuries qualify, medical certification, duration and cost of paid leave, employer and school duties, support services and equality between staff groups.

rows.title: Maternity Protection (Child Bereavement) (Amendment) Bill 2026
rows.what: Would allow a relevant employee to postpone all or part of maternity leave following the death of her child, subject to notification and medical-certification requirements.
rows.practical: The postponed maternity leave could be resumed later as one continuous period, with the Bill allowing postponement for up to 52 weeks from the date it begins under specified conditions.
rows.context: The proposal amends the Maternity Protection Act 1994 so a bereaved mother would not necessarily have to use the remainder of maternity leave immediately after the death of her child.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine eligibility, notice and medical-certificate rules, the maximum postponement period, employment protections and how resumed leave would operate.

rows.title: Regulation of Drones Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill provides for the further regulation of the private and commercial use of unmanned aircraft systems, commonly referred to as drones. The Bill creates new and mandatory planning regulatory considerations under the Planning and Development Act 2024 with respect to the private and commercial.
rows.practical: Within the latter, the Bill requires a planning authority to ensure that private and commercial use of drones is prioritised for purposes in the public interest.
rows.context: The Bill further permits any person, a local authority or the Environmental Protection Agency to make a complaint to the District Court with respect to the emission of noise from certain privately or commercially operated drones.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Harassment, Harmful Communications and Related Offences (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill 2026
rows.what: address these two gaps in the legislative framework.
rows.practical: These offences are provided for by sections 2 and 3 of the Harassment, Harmful Communications and Related Offences Act 2020.
rows.context: Further, the Act does not appear to impose any liability on a social media platform that makes software available to facilitate the generation of such images.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and enforcement.

rows.title: River Boyne Task Force Bill 2023
rows.what: Would establish a River Boyne Task Force within the existing local and regional government framework, with responsibilities for the River Boyne and its catchment area.
rows.practical: The Task Force would coordinate specified functions relating to the Boyne catchment and could make recommendations to planning authorities on the content of development plans.
rows.context: The proposal is intended to create a dedicated structure for coordinating public functions and planning considerations across the River Boyne catchment.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Task Force’s membership, powers, relationship with local authorities, planning role, accountability and resourcing.

rows.title: Agri-Food Regulator (Amendment) Bill 2026
rows.what: The purpose of the Agri-Food Regulator (Amendment) Bill 2026 is to amend.
rows.practical: In practice, the Regulator cannot fulfil its role properly because some retailers are refusing to provide market information voluntarily.
rows.context: The Agri-Food Regulator has been seeking this power since September 2024, following repeated concerns about opaque pricing structures and the inability to verify claims of excessive margins.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Sale of Nitrous Oxide and Related Products Bill 2025
rows.what: To regulate the sale of nitrous oxide products to commercial and medical use only; to enable members of an Garda Síochána to seize nitrous oxide products from those without appropriate licences.
rows.practical: Background There are concerns about the increase in young people misusing Nitrous Oxide.
rows.context: A recent report published by the HSE on their Adolescent Addiction Service has shown that 22% of young people attending their adolescent service admitted to taking Nitrous Oxide on occasion reflecting an increase of 175% compared to 2021.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Equal Status (Access to Toilet Facilities) Bill 2026
rows.what: legislate for such an entitlement along similar lines.
rows.practical: Some bodies provide members with medical access cards or No Wait cards, as a means of requesting urgent access in a discreet way.
rows.context: The conditions are that– • the customer has a “relevant medical condition” as defined, or uses an ostomy device, • three or more members of the staff are working on the premises concerned at the time, 2 • the staff facilities are not in an area where providing access would create an obvious health.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Residential Tenancies (Winter Ban on Evictions) Bill 2025
rows.what: This Bill introduces emergency provision to defer the termination dates of certain residential tenancies that fall, or would fall, during the period beginning on the day after the date of the passing of this Bill and ending on 1 July 2026 in order to mitigate the risk that persons whose tenancies.
rows.practical: Sections 1 and 3 contain standard provisions dealing with the interpretation, short title and collective citation of the Bill.
rows.context: The ‘winter emergency period’ is defined to mean the period commencing on the day after the passing of this Bill and ending on 1 July 2026.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and enforcement.

rows.title: National Minimum Wage (Inclusion of Young Persons, Apprentices and Interns) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would extend the full national minimum hourly rate to employed young people, bring apprentices within the minimum-wage legislation and cover certain interns and work-experience workers.
rows.practical: Age-based reduced rates would be removed for employed young people. Apprentices would be brought into the Acts, while some interns doing more than 30 hours in four weeks would be treated as employees for minimum-wage purposes.
rows.context: The Bill seeks to widen who is protected by the National Minimum Wage Acts, while retaining exceptions for genuine charitable work and prescribed education or training placements.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine the treatment of apprentices and trainees, education-placement exceptions, employer costs, enforcement and the effect of removing age-based minimum-wage rates.

rows.title: Animal Health and Welfare (Ban on Fox Hunting) Bill 2025
rows.what: This is an Act to amend the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013 to ban fox hunting and related practices.
rows.practical: Experience in Britain has shown that a loophole that permits trail hunting – where the scent of a fox is followed – often leads to the pursuit and killing of a fox.
rows.context: Background Fox hunting is a cruel and inhumane blood sport.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Health (Waiting Lists) Bill 2024
rows.what: The Bill would require the Minister for Health to set such priorities and targets.
rows.practical: The Bill provides for greater transparency across all health and social care waiting lists by mandating the collation and report of all such waiting lists by the National Treatment Purchase Fund Board (“NTPF”), which currently only publishes such lists for hospital services.
rows.context: This is in line with the recommendations of the SláinteCare Report to legislate for maximum wait times policies and to legislate for accountability.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Dog Welfare (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: The amendments seek to introduce legislative controls over breeding practices, staff-to-animal ratios, and limitations on breeding to ensure the health and well-being of breeding dogs and their offspring.
rows.practical: The Dog Breeding Establishments Act 2010 established a regulatory framework for the licensing and inspection of premises where dogs are bred.
rows.context: However, concerns have been raised by animal welfare organisations, veterinary professionals, and the general public regarding the conditions under which breeding dogs are kept, the frequency of breeding, and the use of invasive reproductive procedures.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Local Government (Support for Elected Members) Bill 2024
rows.what: Would require a scheme providing administrative support to every elected member of a local authority to help them carry out their duties as public representatives.
rows.practical: The Minister would have to establish the support scheme by regulation. The Bill defines administrative support by reference to the secretarial facilities used for Oireachtas members.
rows.context: The proposal would amend the Local Government Act 2001 so administrative support for councillors becomes a statutory requirement rather than a discretionary arrangement.
rows.issues: Second Stage can consider the level and form of support, costs, staffing and procurement arrangements, consistency across councils and ministerial regulation of the scheme.

rows.title: Electricity (Supply) (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would reduce legal restrictions on ESB works affecting water levels on the Shannon lakes, including Lough Derg, Lough Ree and Lough Allen.
rows.practical: It would remove specified historic water-level limits, allow provision for controlling Lough Ree levels and expressly permit works such as dredging new channels and deepening existing channels.
rows.context: The Bill would amend the Electricity (Supply) (Amendment) (No. 2) Act 1934 to give the ESB greater flexibility in managing lake levels and related works.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine flood management, environmental and ecological impacts, navigation and land impacts, the scope of ESB powers and interaction with modern environmental law.

rows.title: Wind Turbine Regulation Bill 2025
rows.what: regulate wind turbines. It provides limits on exportation of product generated from turbines; provides for protection of nearby dwellings, allows for public consultative processes; and facilitates community ownership.
rows.practical: It provides limits on exportation of product generated from turbines; provides for protection of nearby dwellings, allows for public consultative processes; and facilitates community ownership.
rows.context: regulate wind turbines. It provides limits on exportation of product generated from turbines; provides for protection of nearby dwellings, allows for public consultative processes; and facilitates community ownership.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Seán Lemass Dublin International Airport Bill 2025
rows.what: provide for the renaming of Dublin Airport as Seán Lemass Dublin International Airport . This change is intended to honour the legacy of Seán Lemass, former Taoiseach and a pivotal figure in Ireland’s economic and infrastructural development during the mid-20th century.
rows.practical: This change is intended to honour the legacy of Seán Lemass, former Taoiseach and a pivotal figure in Ireland’s economic and infrastructural development during the mid-20th century.
rows.context: Background Seán Lemass served as Taoiseach from 1959 to 1966 and is widely credited with modernising Ireland’s economy, promoting industrialisation, and fostering international engagement.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Building Energy Rating (BER) Standards for Private Rented Accommodation Bill 2025
rows.what: provide for minimum Building Energy Rating (BER) standards for Private Rented Accommodation and for related matters.
rows.practical: Provides for the Bill to come into force not later than 90 days from its promulgation by the President.
rows.context: Paul Murphy TD, Ruth Coppinger TD, Aibreán, 2025.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, and implementation.

rows.title: Forty-first Amendment of the Constitution (Reduction of Voting Age to Sixteen Years) Bill 2025
rows.what: The ambition of the Forty-first Amendment of the Constitution (Reduction of the V oting Age to Sixteen Years) Bill 2025 is to provide for a legislative pathway for the reduction of the age at which a person may vote from 18 to 16 years of age in this State.
rows.practical: One of the recommendations to come out of the 2012-2014 Convention on the Constitution was to reduce the voting age to 16.
rows.context: Background In the past, there have been campaigns and calls from advocacy groups and others to lower the voting age in this jurisdiction from 18 to 16 years of age.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and constitutional implications.

rows.title: Arts (Recognition of Comedy) (Amendment) Bill 2024
rows.what: Should An Chomhairle Ealaíon could choose to revise this definition, there would be no need for legislation, but by amending the 2003 Act to explicitly recognise comedy as an art form, we can ensure that, in future, the arts cannot be interpreted so as to not include comedy.
rows.practical: As a result of not being mentioned explicitly in the Arts Act 2003, the art of comedy, and the comedians who write and perform, are in effect being excluded from opportunities for arts funding, resources, and development by An Chomhairle Ealaíon (the Arts Council).
rows.context: Aengus Ó Snodaigh sponsors the Bill. The official record does not provide a clean plain-English background summary in the extracted source text.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Emergency Inspection of Dublin Zoo Bill 2025
rows.what: Would require the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage to report on appointing an emergency independent inspector for Dublin Zoo.
rows.practical: The Minister would have to consider and report on an independent emergency inspection rather than leaving the issue solely within existing administrative arrangements.
rows.context: The explanatory memorandum states that the Bill’s purpose is specifically to require a ministerial report on the appointment of an emergency independent inspector for Dublin Zoo.
rows.issues: Second Stage can consider the trigger and scope of an emergency inspection, inspector independence and powers, reporting, animal-welfare oversight and interaction with existing regulators.

rows.title: Companies (Protection of Title: Accountant) Bill 2025
rows.what: Background and Rationale Under current Irish company law, the title “auditor” is protected and only individuals or firms meeting specific qualifications and registration requirements may use it.
rows.practical: However, the title “accountant” remains unregulated, allowing individuals without formal training or professional affiliation to use it freely.
rows.context: This lack of protection can mislead consumers, undermine professional standards, and dilute the credibility of the accountancy profession.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Domestic Violence (Free Travel Scheme) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would require the Minister for Social Protection to establish a free-travel scheme for victims who are fleeing, or have recently fled, domestic violence.
rows.practical: A qualifying pass would normally last three months, with a possible three-month extension, and would provide the same transport access as the existing Free Travel Scheme while not revealing why the pass was issued.
rows.context: Assessments would be carried out by approved bodies after consultation with Cuan, and the Minister would have to report annually to the Oireachtas on use and effectiveness of the scheme.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine eligibility and verification, privacy and safety, duration of support, participating transport services, administration and cost.

rows.title: Industrial Relations (Boycott of Joint Labour Committees) Bill 2025
rows.what: The purpose was to improve terms of employment in the “sweated industries”, where pay was chronically low and union representation was either non-existent or inadequate.
rows.practical: The goal was explicitly to reduce downwards wage competition – where, in the words of Winston Churchill introducing the first Trade Boards Bill, “the good employer is undercut by the bad, and the bad employer is undercut by the worst”.
rows.context: But, on the other hand, compulsory machinery for collective bargaining, through the mechanism of trade boards and subsequently joint labour committees (JLCs), was reserved for sectors in which existing organisation was very weak or non-existent.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Protection of Retail Workers Bill 2025
rows.what: Would create specific public-order offences for assaulting, threatening or abusing a retail worker while that person is engaged in retail work.
rows.practical: A person convicted summarily could face up to 12 months’ imprisonment and/or a fine, with the offence covering both individual incidents and a course of threatening or abusive conduct.
rows.context: The Bill would amend the Criminal Justice (Public Order) Act 1994 and define retail workers broadly enough to include employees, owners, agency staff and people delivering goods from retail premises.
rows.issues: Second Stage can consider the need for a retail-specific offence, definitions, penalties, proof that the accused knew the victim was working, and overlap with existing assault and public-order offences.

rows.title: Wildlife (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: amend the Wildlife Act, 1976 to provide legal protection for the sprat by including it in the Fifth Schedule of the Act.
rows.practical: This would prohibit the targeted fishing of sprat and would place a moratorium on commercial sprat fishing until sufficient scientific data is available regarding its population dynamics, habitat use, and ecological function.
rows.context: Despite its ecological importance, sprat is currently subject to unregulated and intensive commercial fishing in Irish waters, with no species-specific management plan or quota system in place.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Occupying Power (Securities and Handling of Settlement Goods) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill proposes a legal change in the area described by its title: Occupying Power (Securities and Handling of Settlement Goods) Bill 2025.
rows.practical: It provides that the Central Bank shall not approve a prospectus pursuant to the Prospectus Regulation that is issued by or on behalf of an occupying power.
rows.context: The provisions of this Bill are intended to apply generally, but the situation in Israel and the Occupied Palestinian Territories is the immediately relevant context.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Taxes Consolidation (Development of Regional Film Industry) (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill proposes a legal change in the area described by its title: Taxes Consolidation (Development of Regional Film Industry) (Amendment) Bill 2025.
rows.practical: Figures provided by Screen Producers Ireland show that 70 per cent of projects which received section 481 film tax relief in 2024 were based in Leinster and over 54 per cent in the Dublin and Wicklow region which constitutes the major hub for film production capacity.
rows.context: This Bill would allow the Minister to identify regions of low audiovisual capacity and to include measures in the industry development test for Section 481 tax relief to promote the development of audiovisual production outside the existing major production hubs.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Compulsory Purchase Order Bill 2025
rows.what: The Compulsory Purchase Order Bill 2025 aims to modernize and streamline the process of compulsory land acquisition in Ireland. The bill ensures fair compensation for landowners and establishes clear procedures for acquiring authorities, replacing outdated laws with a more efficient and transparent.
rows.practical: The bill ensures fair compensation for landowners and establishes clear procedures for acquiring authorities, replacing outdated laws with a more efficient and transparent system.
rows.context: Background The Law Reform Commission published a report on 29 March 2023.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Road Traffic and Roads (Blood Bikes Exemption) (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: expand the exemption to cover the brave men and women who assist the State through the provision of blood bike services.
rows.practical: This Bill would provide that any exemption granted to ambulances from such traffic restrictions under regulation would apply also to blood bike services.
rows.context: The British government has recognised the role of these front-line services in law and through an exemption from road tax for their vehicles, following campaign efforts of the Nationwide Association of Blood Bikes, which includes a number of member organisations in Ireland.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Coroners (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill proposes a legal change in the area described by its title: Coroners (Amendment) Bill 2025.
rows.practical: Introduction This Bill deals with the issue of Iatrogenic Suicide.
rows.context: change the law to give recognition to this differentiation in relation to a verdict that can be made following an inquest undertaken under the Coroners Act 1962.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and enforcement.

rows.title: Health (Availability of General Practitioner Services) Bill 2025
rows.what: Although it is not fixed by law, it seems that full eligibility for health services will usually extend to about 40% of the population.
rows.practical: As well as the full medical card issued to persons with full eligibility, legislation also provides for a more restricted GP visit card.
rows.context: Broadly, access to primary care services is means-tested and is made available throughout the State to persons who are unable without undue hardship to arrange such services for themselves and their dependants.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Health (Scoliosis Treatment Services) Bill 2024
rows.what: Would require the HSE to establish and maintain a national inpatient and outpatient scoliosis treatment service for children and adults normally resident in the State.
rows.practical: The HSE would have duties to provide adequate specialist staff, facilities and resources, and could arrange treatment outside the State where timely care cannot otherwise be provided.
rows.context: The Bill also requires regular reporting on demand, waiting lists and resources, while the Minister for Health would issue service-time guidelines and lay reports and guidelines before the Oireachtas.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine enforceable treatment timelines, staffing and capacity, funding, use of overseas care, reporting obligations and the respective duties of the HSE and Minister.

rows.title: Animal Health and Welfare (Welfare of Pigs) Bill 2025
rows.what: amend the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013 to improve the welfare of pigs by prohibiting teeth-clipping, tail- docking and castration, limiting the use of tusk reduction and prohibiting sow stalls and farrowing crates of less than 5 metres square.
rows.practical: Prohibits procedures (other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes) that are likely to damage or remove a sensitive part of a pig’s body or alter its bone structure, such as teeth-clipping, tail-docking and castration.
rows.context: Prohibits sow stalls and farrowing crates that do not allow a sow or gilt to turn around and are less than 5 metres square.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and enforcement.

rows.title: Broadcasting (All Ireland Service) (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: RTÉ held an audience competition to win tickets to watch the All- Ireland Football Final, in which Armagh were playing and would go on to win, and yet supporters in Armagh were prohibited from taking part in the competition along with all viewers north of the border.
rows.practical: Background of the Bill “It is the entitlement and birthright of every person born in the island of Ireland, which includes its islands and seas, to be part of the Irish Nation.” – Article 2, Bunreacht na hÉireann.
rows.context: Aengus Ó Snodaigh sponsors the Bill. The official record does not provide a clean plain-English background summary in the extracted source text.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Healthcare (Transparent Payments) Bill 2022
rows.what: This section also mandates the Health Products Regulatory Authority to establish and maintain such a register that is publicly accessible and searchable.
rows.practical: It also provides the HPRA with the power to audit parties involved to ensure compliance with this obligation.
rows.context: Each year millions of euro is paid to health care professionals and health care organisations by pharmaceutical companies and medical equipment suppliers for a range of reasons, including consultancy, research and development, speaking events, data analysis and medical writing.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Criminal Law (Prohibition of the Disclosure of Counselling Records) Bill 2025
rows.what: This is an Act to amend the Criminal Evidence Act 1992 in relation to the disclosure of counselling records in criminal cases for certain offences, namely sexual offences, offences involving coercive control and intimate partner violence. Prior to this Act,.
rows.practical: Prior to this Act, section 19A of the Criminal Evidence Act 1992 established a mechanism for the accused in sexual offences cases to seek disclosure of counselling records of alleged victims.
rows.context: Counselling records are notes and other records taken by counselling professionals while treating a client.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Taxes Consolidation (Rights of Performers and Film Workers) (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would amend the Taxes Consolidation Act 1997 so Section 481 film tax relief certification takes account of equal treatment for Irish performers.
rows.practical: Qualifying productions seeking Section 481 relief would have to meet requirements intended to prevent Irish performers receiving worse intellectual-property terms than international performers.
rows.context: The Bill follows recommendations from the Oireachtas Budgetary Oversight Committee on the operation of the Section 481 industry-development test.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test how equal treatment would be defined, how compliance would be certified and enforced, and the effect on performers and film-production companies.

rows.title: Dereliction and Building Regeneration Bill 2025
rows.what: amend existing legislation in relation to derelict property and the processes of upgrading and regenerating existing property.
rows.practical: The Bill also provides for a national Town Centre First Partnership office to oversee this new process and to assist and provide guidance to all local authorities on the re-use, refurbishment and retrofitting of existing buildings.
rows.context: The amendments relate to: • the definition of derelict buildings for the purposes of placing buildings on the derelict sites register.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Planning And Development (Exempted Development - External Wall Insulation) Bill 2025
rows.what: Would make external wall insulation exempt from planning permission in most cases by amending the Planning and Development Act 2000.
rows.practical: Households could generally install exterior insulation without applying for planning permission, except for protected structures, architectural conservation areas and developments that seriously conflict with proper planning and sustainable development.
rows.context: The Bill is intended to remove a planning barrier to external wall insulation while retaining protections for heritage buildings, conservation areas and exceptional planning impacts.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine heritage safeguards, visual and neighbour impacts, ministerial regulation, consistency with building standards and whether the exemption is sufficiently precise.

rows.title: Equality (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Employment Equality Acts 1998-2021 prohibit discrimination in relation to employment, including vocational training and work experience.
rows.practical: The Equal Status Acts 2000-2018 (‘the Acts’) prohibit discrimination in the provision of goods and services, accommodation and education.
rows.context: The purpose of these amendments is to ensure that persons can no longer be discriminated against on the basis that they come from a disadvantaged socio-economic area or background.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Water Services (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Water Services Amendment Bill 2025 seeks to make amendments to the Water Services (No.2) Act 2013 to give the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) the legislative remit to develop a code of practice for water service outages and interruptions and to establish a dispute resolution.
rows.practical: It provides that it shall come into operation on such day or days as the Minister may by order; and such day or days shall not be later than 3 months from the date on which the Act is signed into law.
rows.context: Introduction The Water Services Amendment Bill 2025 seeks to make amendments to the Water Services (No.2) Act 2013 to give the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) the legislative remit to develop a code of practice for water service outages and interruptions and to establish a dispute.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Public Health (Restriction on Sale of Stimulant Drinks to Children) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill proposes a legal change in the area described by its title: Public Health (Restriction on Sale of Stimulant Drinks to Children) Bill 2025.
rows.practical: It will be an offence for a person to contravene this prohibition.
rows.context: Parental or guardian consent in writing will be required where a minor is engaged to act as a test purchaser and in all cases and all reasonable steps must be taken to protect the young person concerned.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Children’s Health (Ospidéal Náisiúnta Kathleen Lynn do Leanaí) (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: This Bill would formally name the new National Children’s Hospital in honour of pioneering medic, suffragette and republican, Dr. Kathleen Lynn TD, who founded Ireland’s first infant hospital, Teach Naomh Ultáin, and served as the only woman commandant in the 1916 Rising.
rows.practical: Lynn established as the nation’s first children’s hospital in 1919.
rows.context: Background of the Bill This Bill is based on one first introduced in Seanad Éireann by then Senator Fintan Warfield in March 2024, as well as amendments previously proposed to the Children’s Health Act 2018 by Louise O’Reilly TD and Aengus Ó Snodaigh TD.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and costs and resourcing.

rows.title: Guardianship of Infants (Amendment) Bill 2025
rows.what: The Bill provides for the introduction of an interim suspension of guardianship rights immediately on conviction, with exceptions allowed for in certain cases of manslaughter where it would not be in the interests of justice to proceed.
rows.practical: The Bill allocates responsibility to the Child and Family Agency to apply for a full suspension of guardianship rights and provides powers to the District Court to order a full suspension of guardian rights where it is in the best interests of the child and where another guardian is available.
rows.context: The Guardian Ad Litem will submit a report on the views of the child to the Court, as well as their own recommendations and the reasoning for these recommendations.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and safeguards for children.

rows.title: Health (Postponement of Certain Leave) Bill 2024
rows.what: Would allow maternity leave or adoptive leave to be postponed where the person taking the leave is diagnosed with, or undergoing treatment for, cancer.
rows.practical: A worker could request to return to work and preserve the unused portion of qualifying leave for a later continuous period after being certified fit to return, subject to rules set by legislation and regulation.
rows.context: The Bill amends both the Maternity Protection Act 1994 and Adoptive Leave Act 1995 so serious cancer treatment does not necessarily consume a person’s statutory family leave entitlement.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine eligibility, employer consent and notice, medical evidence, maximum postponement periods, interaction with sick leave and protections when resumed leave begins.

rows.title: Clean Air (Smoky Coal Ban) Bill 2021
rows.what: of the Act, to prohibit the sale, marketing, distribution and burning of bituminous (smoky) coal, on a nationwide basis. 2 The existing regulations, made by Ministers exercising their powers under the Air Pollution Act 1987 (S.I. 326/2012 and S.I. 260/2020), shall be amended by the current Minister.
rows.practical: This Bill is designed to require the Minister introduce to extend the Low Smoke Zones to cover the entire country, thereby creating a nationwide ban on the use of smoky coal.
rows.context: The majority of Ireland is not covered by Low Smoke Zones and due to the patch work nature of the existing ban, there is very significant use of smoky coal in areas that are currently designated as Low Smoke Zones.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, oversight, and enforcement.

rows.title: Thirty-ninth Amendment of the Constitution (Judicial Oath of Office) Bill 2025
rows.what: This will avoid the risk that it either excludes any person taking the oath, or could be construed as limiting the obligations on a judge to any one section of society.
rows.practical: Schedule – the Schedule of the Bill provides the text of the amendment to Article 34 of Bunreacht na hÉireann: Part 1 provides the Irish language text of the amendment; Part 2 provides the English language text of the amendment.
rows.context: Leis sin, seachnófar an baol go n-eisiafar leis aon duine a ghlacfaidh an mionn, nó go bhféadfaí é a fhorléiriú mar ní lena ndéantar na hoibleagáidí atá ar bhreitheamh a theorannú d’aon chuid ar leith den tsochaí.
rows.issues: Second Stage can test the Bill’s overall approach, including scope and definitions, implementation, and constitutional implications.

rows.title: Domestic Violence (Amendment) (No. 3) Bill 2024
rows.what: Would broaden who can be treated as a “relevant person” for the offence of coercive control under the Domestic Violence Act 2018.
rows.practical: The offence could apply across a wider set of relationships, including current or former intimate partners, specified relatives and certain people connected through guardianship of a child.
rows.context: The Bill responds to the existing relationship definition in section 39 of the 2018 Act and also provides a limited defence for conduct reasonably believed to be in the relevant person’s best interests, except for specified behaviour.
rows.issues: Second Stage can examine how far the relationship definition should extend, the scope of the defence, evidential thresholds and protection against coercive control outside former partner relationships.
